floor_history.headline: Recon complete: floor 20/158 is purely two RA permutation clusters (v1@$2-vs-$3 cascade ~16 insns; a0_58/a1_val $4-$5 tie 4 insns); zero structural diffs; 3 probes measured (2 byte-neutral, 1 worse)

frontier.hypothesis: Cluster 1 closes when v1 loses $2 to the table-pointer chain (H1, ~16 of 20)
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 global/local alloc priority between the multi-block v1 pseudo and arm-local table temps
frontier.next_probe: Run the -da greg dump (register-alloc-pure-c Step-0) on the sandbox .i to read actual allocno priorities for v1 vs table temps, THEN steer: separate named local for the shifted index per arm (sanctioned named-intermediate order) so v1's pseudo dies early, or reuse-variable spelling on the table chain to lift its refs

frontier.hypothesis: Cluster 2 closes by merging a0_58 and v1_58 into ONE reused variable loaded twice from s0+0x58 (H2, 4 of 20)
frontier.mechanism: 4-ref reused pseudo outranks a1_val in allocno priority, winning $4 as in target (variable-reuse family, SOTN-sanctioned)
frontier.next_probe: p = *(s32*)(s0+0x58); ... *(u8*)p ...; p = *(s32*)(s0+0x58); *(u8*)(p+2) — verify insn count stays 158 and cluster-2 diff flips

frontier.hypothesis: Else-arm idx register and addu operand orders are pure cascade of H1 (H3)
frontier.mechanism: register identity, not C operand order, decides the emitted addu operand order
frontier.next_probe: no separate probe — verify automatically when H1 lands
